title: The server rejects your push: file exceeds the size limit
summary: A dataset was committed four commits ago and the server refuses the whole branch. Deleting it now does not help — you must remove it from the commit that added it, then push.
mental_model: The server validates every object in the push, not just the final tree. A large blob in any commit of the branch fails the whole push, so the fix must remove it from that commit — not add a later one that deletes the file.

write.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Reject any push containing a blob over the size limit.
LIMIT=120000
ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
status=0

while read old new ref; do
  [ "$new" = "$ZERO" ] && continue
  if [ "$old" = "$ZERO" ]; then
    range="$new"
  else
    range="$old..$new"
  fi
  for sha in $(git rev-list --objects $range 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1); do
    type=$(git cat-file -t "$sha" 2>/dev/null) || continue
    [ "$type" = "blob" ] || continue
    size=$(git cat-file -s "$sha" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "$size" -gt "$LIMIT" ]; then
      name=$(git rev-list --objects $range | grep "^$sha" | cut -d' ' -f2-)
      echo "pre-receive: $name is $size bytes, over the $LIMIT limit" >&2
      status=1
    fi
  done
done

[ "$status" -ne 0 ] && echo "pre-receive: push rejected. Remove the file from history, not just from the tip." >&2
exit $status

setup.run: git commit -q -m "Add the sample dataset for testing"

commit.message: Use a context manager in the importer

steps.title: Watch the push get rejected
steps.why: The server checks every object in the push, so the branch fails as a whole. Read the message: it names the file and the commit range, which is everything you need.
steps.expect: remote: pre-receive: sample-data.csv is 2xxxxx bytes, over the limit.

verify.label: the branch was rejected by the server

steps.title: Try the fix everyone tries first
steps.why: Deleting the file and committing does not help: the blob is still in the commit that added it, and the push still contains that commit. This is the key misunderstanding the whole scenario exists to correct.
steps.expect: Rejected again, for the same object.

verify.label: deleting at the tip did not help
verify.hint: the blob is still inside an earlier commit in the push

steps.title: Find which commit introduced it
steps.why: `--diff-filter=A` names the commit that added the file. That is the commit that must be rewritten — nothing else will do.
steps.expect: One commit, and the blob still reachable from the branch.

steps.title: Remove it from every commit on the branch
steps.why: `filter-branch` limited to `main..HEAD` rewrites only your unpushed commits — the shared history on main is untouched, which is what makes this rewrite safe to do unilaterally.
steps.expect: Three commits, none of them containing the dataset.

verify.cmd: sh -c 'git rev-list --objects main..HEAD | grep sample-data | wc -l'
verify.label: no commit on the branch carries the dataset any more
verify.hint: git filter-branch --index-filter with a main..HEAD range

steps.title: Prevent it happening again in the same branch
steps.why: Ignore the path before pushing, so a colleague regenerating the dataset does not repeat the incident. Fixing the history without fixing the cause guarantees a second occurrence.

write.content:
# Generated test data — regenerate locally, never commit.
sample-data.csv
*.csv

steps.title: Push successfully
steps.why: Every object in the push is now under the limit, so the hook passes. Note the branch's commits all have new shas — acceptable precisely because nobody had ever received them.

verify.label: the cleaned branch pushed successfully

steps.why: Read the branch from the bare repository: the importer and its tests are there, the dataset is not, and no giant object was ever transferred.

verify.label: the server's copy has no trace of the dataset
the branch is published

verify.label: the real work reached the server

verify.cmd: sh -c 'git rev-list --objects feature/import | grep sample-data | wc -l'

the cause was fixed as well as the symptom

pitfalls: A later commit that deletes the file does not help. The push contains every commit, and the server validates every object in it.
Rewriting is safe here only because the branch was never accepted by the server. If it had been pushed and pulled, coordinate first.
GitHub's hard limit is 100MB per file, with warnings above 50MB, and it applies to any object in the push — not just the tip.
The real fix is a pre-commit size check plus .gitignore. By the time the server rejects it, you are already doing history surgery.
If the dataset is genuinely needed, Git LFS or an artefact store is the answer — not a bigger limit.
